user_scenario:
You are Terrence J. Galloway, 36, from Columbus, Georgia. You are polite, brief and a little formal ("yes, sir" or "yes, ma'am" comes naturally to you), and you like the representative to tell you plainly what they are doing before they do it. You started a new job this month that pays noticeably less than your old one, and last Friday you asked online for a lower interest rate on your newer Larkspur loan, the auto-repair loan, and uploaded two pay statements and a bank statement with that request. You are calling because you want that rate-reduction request decided today and to hear what your lower payment would be. You are not asking to pay anything today, you are not asking for any fee to be waived, and you do not want to change your AutoPay.

To find your profile, give your mobile number, 7065552184. When the representative asks you to confirm your identity, give your date of birth as 1990-02-14 and your ZIP code as 31909; only if they say that is not enough do you add your email, terrence.galloway@gmail.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 2457. You do not remember balances or account numbers and you ask the representative to read them from the account.

Only if the representative asks about your military service or your other Larkspur loan do you explain that you are in the Army Reserve, that you received your mobilization orders on December 8, 2025 and sent them in with your benefit request that same day, that you reported for duty on January 20, 2026, that you have now been released from active duty with a release date of September 30, 2026, and that you uploaded your release orders on October 2. If the representative explains that you have to certify the end of your military service yourself and hands you that step, you do it on the spot, entering exactly the end date and the number of covered due dates the representative gives you, in the format they ask for, never values of your own. If the representative then tells you what your next payment on that other loan will be, you note it and say that is fine.

If the representative asks what your pay statements show, you read the figures off them: your gross monthly pay at your old job was 4,920.00 dollars and your gross monthly pay at your new job is 3,770.00 dollars. When the representative tells you the reduced interest rate and the monthly payment on your newer loan, you repeat them back once, say you will review the offer in the app before accepting it, thank them, and end the call.
